newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIA KOTHARI PIONEER SEES BROAD-BASED STOCKS RISE.
newsitem.headline: INDIA KOTHARI PIONEER SEES BROAD-BASED STOCKS RISE.

text.p: Indian shares are likely to show a better performance compared to fixed income investments with many factors aiding a stocks rally, Kothari Pioneer Asset Management Company Ltd said.

"Shares are likely to perform well and should deliver higher returns than fixed income investments over the next 2-3 years," Kothari said in its annual investment review obtained by Reuters on Monday.
Kothari AMC is the Indian affiliate of Pioneer Group of the United States.

"The catalyst should come from overseas with many foreign funds seeking to increase their India weighting by channeling more assets to us. As is well known, a small drop for them is a big ocean for us," the firm said.

Easing of redemption pressures faced by major domestic mutual funds, an expected improvement in corporate profitability after a reduction in interest rates and the return of domestic investors will lead to a broad-based rally in share prices, Kothari added.

"During this process, we believe that the time will soon come when the large-cap stocks become so overvalued that it will make compelling sense to look at the next tier of slightly less liquid, medium-sized company shares."
The net asset value of Kothari Pioneer's Bluechip Fund stood at 14.16 rupees as on July 15, up 13 percent since April 1, 1997 compared to a 23 percent rise in the BSE index, the firm said.
